before.value: Role-based access with item-specific controls; users are blocked cleanly when their role or item-level permission does not allow viewing, downloading, or editing an object or its metadata. The system should explain denial in plain language without exposing hidden details, and where possible guide users to the next step, such as requesting access or contacting the appropriate staff group. Public users should get a simple, non-technical message that the item isn’t available to view or download due to rights or access restrictions, and if there is a legitimate path to request access, the message should point to it; otherwise it can just explain that the content is restricted. Library staff should get a more specific message that directs them to the correct internal contact or workflow when their role doesn’t allow the action, without revealing anything sensitive about the item itself. Public users may see only basic descriptive information but not the file itself; staff may be able to view a record but not edit or publish it. If rights status is unclear, public access should be restricted until authorized staff verify the status; if rights are mixed, the most restrictive applicable rule governs public visibility, while staff may retain broader internal access if allowed. Readiness checks should confirm that authorized staff can create and edit metadata, ingest or update objects, and assign rights or access settings without needing manual data fixes outside the system. They should also verify consistent enforcement for public users, NIH staff, and repository staff, including restricted, mixed, or unpublished materials, and prove that the same item appears differently depending on user role and rights status, with results staying correct after updates. Public search and viewing should stay available during spikes as long as the system can safely support it; if throttling is needed for stability, it should protect the system first and favor authenticated staff for administrative functions while keeping public discovery and viewing available as much as possible. When preservation and access rules conflict, preserve the content safely but do not expose it publicly until the rights decision is final; preferably show only a minimal restricted representation such as a metadata record or placeholder if staff want the item discoverable without revealing the content, and if even that is too risky, hide it from general users and make it visible only to authorized staff until resolved.
